b1.note: Mechanism is the 'cross-origin isolated' state; COOP(same-origin)+COEP(require-corp) is the standard route, COEP:credentialless is an alternative in Chromium. Desktop Chrome also ran a legacy allowlist of origins permitted SAB without COI, being phased out. SAB was globally disabled (Spectre) in 2018 and re-enabled behind COI in Firefox 79 / Chrome 92 / Safari 15.2.

b2.verdict: disagree: timestamp-query is not exposed to ordinary content by default in Chrome; it is gated behind chrome://flags/#enable-webgpu-developer-features (WebGPU Developer Features), and the app must additionally request the 'timestamp-query' feature on GPUDevice creation or the request fails.
b2.note: Chrome has discussed permission/policy-based exposure for content, but as of my knowledge (early 2025) the flag gate had not been lifted. webgpureport.org shows the feature only when the flag is enabled.

b3.note: Mechanism: in a non-COI document, new WebAssembly.Memory({shared:true}) throws, and compiling/instantiating a module that declares or imports a shared memory fails with a TypeError whose message names cross-origin isolation — observable as a compile/validation failure even though the wasm byte validation itself is not the thing that rejects.

rows.claim: SharedArrayBuffer is exposed only to cross-origin-isolated documents (COOP same-origin + COEP require-corp, or COEP:credentialless in Chromium); a legacy desktop-Chrome origin allowlist permitted SAB without COI but was deprecated.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN SharedArrayBuffer page and 'cross-origin isolation' guide; Chrome developer blog 'Enabling SharedArrayBuffer' articles
rows.notes: Worker contexts inherit COI state from their creating document; non-document contexts (Electron, Node) exempt.

rows.claim: SharedArrayBuffer requires cross-origin isolation (COOP+COEP); exposed only in COI documents since Firefox 79 (July 2020).
rows.verifier_hint: MDN SharedArrayBuffer browser-compat table; Firefox release notes 79
rows.notes: Firefox does not support the COEP:credentialless shortcut as of my knowledge; require-corp is the path.

rows.claim: SharedArrayBuffer requires cross-origin isolation since Safari 15.2 (Dec 2021), where it shipped alongside WebAssembly threads.
rows.verifier_hint: Safari 15.2 release notes (WebKit blog); MDN SharedArrayBuffer compat
rows.notes: Safari supports COEP:require-corp; credentialless support was absent as of my knowledge.

rows.notes: Compute is the core WGSL stage model — available wherever WebGPU ships; adapter limits apply.

rows.claim: COI is per-document and not inherited: a cross-origin iframe must set its own COOP/COEP headers (and all its subresources need CORP/CORS) to become COI; WebGPU itself does not require COI, so an embedded cross-origin iframe can use WebGPU regardless of isolation state.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN 'cross-origin isolation' guide (nested/iframe sections); Chrome developer blog on COOP/COEP with iframes
rows.notes: Exact delegation mechanics for nested COI frames (allow attributes/policy) are the least-settled part; verify against current Chrome docs.

rows.claim: Same per-document model: an embedded cross-origin iframe does not inherit COI and must carry its own COOP/COEP; SAB/threads are gated per frame. WebGPU (Windows, Firefox 137+) does not require COI, so an iframe can use it.
rows.verifier_hint: MDN cross-origin isolation guide; Firefox COOP/COEP documentation

rows.claim: Same per-document COI model; an iframe needs its own COOP/COEP to be isolated (Safari 16.4+ improved frame-level COOP/COEP handling); WebGPU (Safari 18+) does not require COI, so iframes can use it.
rows.verifier_hint: Safari 16.4/18 release notes on COOP/COEP; WebKit cross-origin isolation documentation
rows.notes: Safari's frame-level COI edge cases are the area I am least certain about.
